availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

Fix agent completed count always showing 0 — aggregate from session history
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KK2SHYWMQAPBM0W7T7S3A9FY
Type:      task
Status:    needs_work
Priority:  2
Automation: eligible

─── Description ───
  Agent cards show Active: 0, Completed: 0 because the completed count is only tracked in ephemeral page state via WebSocket events — it resets on page reload and the API never provides initial counts. Fix: (1) In daemon GET /api/agent/status endpoint (agent-dispatch.ts), query session store to aggregate completed session counts by agent_id, (2) return per-agent counts in agent_definitions array (e.g. completed_sessions: number), (3) in agents page, pre-populate completedCounts from API response on load instead of starting from {}. The active count works because it derives from active_invocations — completed needs the same server-side source of truth.
Spec ref:  @ui-agent-dispatch
Tags:      bug, web-ui, daemon
Created:   2026-03-07T00:01:03.380Z
Started:   2026-03-07T03:18:02.122Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent and Dispatch View
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
  and active invocations with links to session streams.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: The /agents route

    When: Agent definitions exist in meta

    Then: Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count

  [ac-2]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The agents page renders

    Then: Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream

  [ac-3]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped

    When: The agents page renders

    Then: Dispatch status shows as stopped with no active invocations

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent definition card on the /agents page
    When: The user clicks the edit icon on the card
    Then: An inline form or modal opens allowing editing of all agent fields (name, description, adapter, dispatch triggers, capabilities, tools, skills, budget, concurrency, auto_approve, prompt_template). Saving persists changes via API and updates the card.

─── Notes ───
[2026-03-07T03:25:58.651Z] @claude:
Fix: agent completed count was always 0 because it was only tracked in ephemeral page state via WebSocket events.

Changes:
1. Added getCompletedSessionCountsByAgent() to src/sessions/store.ts — reads session metadata (not events.jsonl) to count completed sessions per agent_id
2. Updated daemon GET /api/agent/status to include completed_sessions in agent_definitions array
3. Updated web-ui agents page to pre-populate completedCounts from API response on load; WebSocket events still increment for real-time updates
4. Added 4 unit tests for the new function (empty, per-agent counts, non-completed excluded, agent_type fallback)

All 3907+ tests pass. Pre-existing failures in core-skill-install and enhanced-setup tests are unrelated.
[2026-03-07T03:31:27.950Z] Jacob Chapel:
Review findings: MUST-FIX — Spec AC coverage gate failed for @ui-agent-dispatch. kspec validate --json reports missing own AC coverage on this spec (Uncovered: ac-4). There are no // AC: @ui-agent-dispatch ac-4 annotations in tests (checked packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/agents.spec.ts and tests/). The implementation change for completed count looks correct, but review cannot pass until ac-4 has explicit test coverage annotation and validation warning is cleared for this spec.
[2026-03-07T03:31:30.198Z] Jacob Chapel:
